radiology_report:
Amsterdam UMC (location VUmc)
Radiology Dept
Date: 10 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (12.6 ng/mL) and prior biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma. Request for staging and lesion characterization.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 104.0 mL. On T2-weighted imaging, a focal hypo-intense lesion is identified in the peripheral zone, mid right. The lesion measures approximately 12 x 10 mm. On diffusion-weighted imaging, the lesion demonstrates marked restricted diffusion with low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging shows early and intense enhancement of the same region. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or distant metastases are seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the peripheral zone, mid right.
PSAD: 0.13 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.80894667.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 5.6 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Given the rising PSA trend, a referral to urology was made for further evaluation and potential biopsy.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (earliest available):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The tumour is characterized by well-defined tubules and is located in the peripheral zone, mid right. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified.

Summary of trajectory:
Histological findings across the available biopsy timepoints remain stable at ISUP grade group 1.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
